subject: Decision request: on-prem pilot architecture and staffing for VPC/private deployments
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Moreno <elena@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Decision request: on-prem pilot architecture and staffing for VPC/private deployments

Team —

Following the sales kickoff with Acme Analytics last week, they want a short pilot to validate an on-prem/VPC private deployment pattern. We need a cross-functional decision on architecture preference and a confirmed staffing plan so we can give Acme an exact timeline and fixed-cost pilot quote.

High-level ask: choose "Path A" (Redwood-managed VPC with dedicated nodes in customer cloud) vs "Path B" (on-prem package deployed to customer-owned GPUs) for the pilot and confirm the minimal staffing commitments for a 6-week engagement.

Key context and constraints:
- Security: Acme requires customer-managed KMS, audit logs retention for 1 year, and control-plane isolation (they asked for an air-gapped option if possible).
- Timeline: Acme wants a pilot start window the week of 7/18; internal kickoff the week prior.
- Success criteria: end-to-end inference at <120ms p95 for 1k qps steady-state for a 30k token/day workload; audited logs and SLA for data retention.

Options (short):
1) Path A — Managed VPC in Acme account: Redwood provisions dedicated instances in their VPC, we handle runtime, KV cache, autoscaling. Pros: faster, lower ops burden, better rollback. Cons: requires cross-account networking and KMS integration; limited for strict air-gap cases.
2) Path B — On-prem appliance: Customer provides GPU hosts; we deliver a packaged runtime (container + installer) and remote ops support. Pros: meets strict data residency/air-gap; Cons: slower onboarding, higher ops headcount, still some residual remote telemetry concerns.

Attached: vpc-pilot-scope.pdf (scope doc) and staffing-costs.xlsx (ballpark FTE + schedule). Also linked INF-4123 in JIRA for infra work.

Staffing ask (minimal):
- 0.5 PM (pilot coordination) — already covered by me
- 1 Solutions Architect (pre-deploy + runbook) — 2 wks frontload, 1 wk validation
- 1 Infra Engineer / deployment lead (3 wks) — install, tuning, quant/profile ops
- 1 SRE on-call (rotated across pilot, 24/7 cover for production-facing incidents)
- Security contact for KMS & audit configuration (audit + attestation)

Decision deadline: EOD Thursday 2027-07-01 so we can finalize statement of work and quote.

Please reply with preferred path, any blockers, and firm confirmation on the staffing items above. If Path B, call out any minimum HW SKUs that are non-negotiable.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

——
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Decision request: on-prem pilot architecture and staffing for VPC/private deployments

Mina — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifying questions before I give a preference: 

- KMS: does Acme require us to integrate with their customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for both keys and envelope encryption, or will a dedicated customer KMS account used by Redwood be acceptable? If BYOK is required, we need a quick security design review (timeline impact: ~4 business days).
- Air-gap: when you say "air-gapped option," do they expect zero outbound telemetry? If yes, Path B is the only viable route.
- Rollback/fallback: if we start Path A and hit a hard compliance block, how fast can we pivot to Path B? Need an estimate for rollback cost & time.

I lean toward Path A if BYOK + KMS integration meets their policy because it's faster, but I want the Sec/Infra answers above before locking. Marcus — can you confirm the pivot cost/time? Karthik — can you flag any infra-level gating items (network adjacency, firewall policies, required node types)?

Cc'ing Elena to keep Acme in the loop — hi Elena, quick note: we may propose the managed VPC approach if it satisfies KMS/audit constraints; we want to confirm whether BYOK is a hard constraint.

– Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

Quick technical notes from infra: 

- Pivot time A -> B:
  * Best-case (automation + playbook ready): 3 working days to get runtime running in customer infra assuming HW is ready and network is pre-approved.
  * Typical-case: 7–10 working days if we have to coordinate on firewall rules, reachability, and KMS handoffs.
  * Cost: roughly 2x effort (additional 1 extra Infra Eng for 2 weeks + extra on-call cycles). See staffing-costs.xlsx for line items.

- Minimum HW (Path B):
  * 4x A100/80GB or equivalent (mixed 40–80GB acceptable if model can be sharded); smaller cards will require model quantization and may not meet latency targets.
  * 256GB RAM per host, NVMe for KV/cache; 10GbE private network between nodes recommended.

- On-call / ops: one SRE is enough for the pilot if on-call is limited to business hours + on-call pager escalation overnight. If Acme wants 24/7 direct coverage from Redwood, add +0.5 FTE SRE (rotational).

I'll add a short runbook (INF-4123) and populate the staffing sheet with exact FTE days.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Decision request: on-prem pilot architecture and staffing for VPC/private deployments

Thanks all — pulling this together into a single decision ask for leadership: 

Summary of constraints and recommended path:
- Acme has indicated BYOK is preferred; they can provide a KMS account that Redwood will be able to call into (no HSM handoff required).
- Security: Acme expects no outbound telemetry to 3rd-party analytics; they will review an allowlist for minimal telemetry (health checks and aggregated metrics only).
- Marcus confirms pivot A->B is possible but costs an extra Infra Eng and ~1 week. Minimum HW for Path B is 4x A100-class GPUs with 256GB RAM per host.

Recommendation: Proceed with Path A (managed VPC in customer account) conditional on a short security integration sprint to validate BYOK flow (4 business days) and a narrowed telemetry allowlist. This reduces onboarding time and lowers pilot cost for Acme; we commit to a documented pivot plan (INF-4123) with a cost/time contingency.

Staffing confirmation requested (yes/no):
- Solutions Architect: 1 FTE (2 weeks frontload) — required
- Infra Engineer (deployment lead): 1 FTE (3 weeks) — required
- SRE on-call: 0.5–1.0 FTE depending on shift coverage — prefer 0.5 for pilot

Decision requested from Karthik and Alex by EOD 2027-07-01: approve Path A with the conditional sec sprint + staffing commitments so we can lock the SoW for Acme.

Meeting: scheduling a 30m sync Thu 7/1 at 10:00am PT to confirm — invite to follow.

Elena — we'll confirm the BYOK design next week and share an updated SoW by 7/8 if approved.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
